title: Top 5 tips for vibe coding an iOS app with Claude Code
description: Five tips for vibe coding an iOS app with Claude Code: how to scope the build, handle Expo quirks, debug with agents, keep context clean, and ship faster than a traditional dev cycle.
transcript: Here's my top five tips and tricks for building an iOS app with Claude code. Number one is traditionally iOS apps are written in Swift, which almost all LLMs are terrible at. So, instead you should use a React Native framework called Expo. Expo allows you to build your mobile app in React, which LLMs know really well, and Expo has their own MCP server, which allows your agent to autonomously test your mobile app on the iOS simulator. Number two is configuring payments in your mobile app can be really painful, so using something called RevenueCat makes it much more seamless, allows you to have an integrated dashboard all of your pricing analytics, as well as an MCP server to connect your agent so it can configure payments for you. Number three, one of the most annoying parts of creating a mobile app is configuring payments and other metadata in App Store Connect. Lucky for you, there is an App Store Connect MCP server that allows your agent to configure all of that metadata in App Store Connect autonomously for you. Number four, the most important part of your mobile app if you want to make money from it is your paywall screen. And if you want to do this correctly, install a software in your mobile app called Superwall, which allows you to remotely AB test different paywalls to optimize conversion rates. Number five, the second most important part of your app if you want to make money from it is your onboarding sequence. And if you want to monitor how your users actually travel through that onboarding sequence, when they convert or when they go off the app, install something called Posthog to actually measure the analytics of how users navigate through your app. If you want to learn more about using Agentic AI tools not only to create mobile apps, but to create all types of software and automate your business, I host full Claude code masterclasses and fundamentals courses in my school community. The link is in my bio, and I would love to see you there.
